title: observability: token-level cost/latency dashboard refinements + alert tuning and KV cache metrics
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Users reported noisy token-level cost and latency alerts during normal traffic spikes and lacked visibility into KV cache behavior. This PR refines dashboard layouts, adds additional KV-cache-specific metrics, and tunes alert thresholds to reduce false positives while keeping signal for regressions. Changes include: 1) dashboard: re-layout token-cost/latency dashboards to surface per-model and per-route percentiles (p50/p95/p99), and add an aggregated per-token cost heatmap; 2) metrics: expose new telemetry for KV cache hit/miss by route and by model_variant, and add a derived metric for effective tokens-per-GPU-hour; 3) alerting: adjust existing alert rules to use rate-limited windows, use p95 for latency regressions, and add a burn-rate style alert for sustained increases in per-token cost; 4) tracing/logging: add trace tags for cache_hit/cache_lookup_time and ensure traces sample at higher rate for long-tail token latency draws; 5) ops: migration script to backfill KV cache metrics for the last 7 days to seed dashboards. Testing: local unit tests for metric name changes, integration test wiring dashboards to mock metrics, and manual validation against prod-like traffic in perf-canary. Rollout plan: feature-gated metrics exposed behind feature flag "obs.token_kv_enhancements" for 48h canary in us-west-2; alerts will be staged to a muted channel for 24h and then enabled for on-call. See checklist below. Checklist: - [x] Metrics instrumentation added and unit tested; - [x] Dashboard JSONs updated and visually validated; - [x] Alert tuning reviewed with SRE and runbook updated; - [x] Backfill script created and dry-run validated; - [x] Docs updated (redwood-docs observability section). Related: ENG-4672 (dashboard rework), SRE-189 (alert noise reduction).
